page: Microsoft Azure HB120-16rs_v3 is a specialized high-performance computing virtual machine configured under Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the server provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs with dedicated physical resource allocation. It offers an asymmetrical compute-to-memory footprint featuring 456 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 28.5 GB per vCPU. Fast local scratch space is provided via a bundled 2435 GB NVMe solid-state drive, complemented by Premium Storage compatibility. The configuration includes zero GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Belonging to the HBv3 family within Azure HPC offerings, this configuration supports Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking. RDMA enables low-latency, high-throughput node-to-node communication across clustered environments, offloading communication overhead from the CPU cores. While the underlying host platform is designed around 120 vCPUs, this specific instance exposes only 16 cores, directing the balance of host memory and IO bandwidth toward this smaller execution pool.

The primary trade-off of this configuration is lower total compute parallelism compared to full-socket instances, counterbalanced by elevated per-core memory bandwidth and capacity. From an infrastructure cost perspective, this profile provides high cost efficiency for workloads governed by per-core software licensing models, allowing organizations to avoid licensing unneeded vCPUs while accessing enterprise-grade memory scale and high-speed NVMe storage. The HB120-16rs_v3 is suited for memory-bound simulation modeling, large in-memory database engines, high-volume ETL processing, and compute-restricted scientific analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure HB120-16rs_v3 is a high-performance computing virtual machine designed for memory-intensive computational tasks. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the server provides 16 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs backed by an Intel processor. A core feature of this instance is its exceptional memory density, delivering 456 GB of system RAM, which translates to 28.5 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities also include 2435 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage and support for RDMA networking alongside Azure Premium Storage. The server operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By concentrating massive memory allocation across a reduced core count, the instance maximizes cost efficiency for licenses billed on a per-core basis while avoiding resource contention. The HB120-16rs_v3 is well matched for large-footprint in-memory databases, memory-bound high-performance computing simulations, data analysis, and advanced ETL pipelines requiring substantial per-thread memory capacity.
